original_recipe.constraint_classification: Assumed simulated oxygen operating limit, not measured product quality.
original_recipe.mass_definition: Terminal product inventory P[g/L]*V[L]/1000. No harvest occurs before96h; stopped batches count zero produced/released product.

evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52.0 h = 12.03 mg/L (online sensor), far above 2.0 mg/L minimum; historical minimum ~9.3 mg/L near t=24 h
Receiving P assay: 0.977 g/L at 36 h, 2.843 g/L at 48 h (available at 52 h), matching source batches (2.98-3.06 g/L at 48 h) within ~5%
Receiving DO2 trajectory (drop ~24 h, recovery ~28 h, ~12-13 plateau) matches the three source batch patterns
Source batches peak at P ~8.0-8.4 g/L at 72 h then slightly decline; receiving is on a similar course with slight lag
Steep product slope (0.98 -> 2.84 g/L over 12 h) argues against feed reduction or stop
submission.rationale: No intervention needed. DO2 is ~12 mg/L with 6x margin above the 2.0 mg/L constraint, product titer (2.84 g/L at 48 h) matches the source calibration envelope within ~5%, and the DO2 trajectory reproduces the healthy source pattern. Interventions would either cut product mass during the steepest production phase or add unneeded aeration; KEEP preserves full productivity and retains all product mass.
submission.uncertainty: Receiving lags sources by roughly half a step in the DO2 pattern, so the final peak may occur slightly later (~76 h) and be a few percent lower; hidden kinetic parameters could alter this. However, no evidence of oxygen limitation, stall, or byproduct degradation exists, and assay noise (~0.02 g/L early) is negligible at current titers. An extra assay was declined because the 48 h assay plus online DO2 already give sufficient confidence.

evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52.0 h = 12.03 mg/L, far above minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0, no declining trend toward a constraint
Receiving P assay at t=48 h (available 52.0 h) = 2.843 g/L, consistent with source batches source-1 (3.057), source-2 (3.017), source-3 (2.979) at same age
Receiving trajectory matches all three source batches' lag/growth patterns (e.g., dip near 24 h, recovery at 28 h), indicating a healthy, in-family run
No measurement anomalies or stalls in receiving DO2/P history up to the 52 h decision time
submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation shows no anomaly: DO2 is ~12 mg/L at t=52 h (vs 2.0 mg/L minimum), and the delayed product assay P(48h)=2.84 g/L matches the source batches (~2.98–3.06 g/L) at the same process age. Growth is on the normal trajectory. Reducing feed or stopping would sacrifice product mass; increasing air is unnecessary since no oxygen constraint is approached. Any bounded intervention here adds risk without expected benefit, so the least-risk, mass-retaining action is to keep conditions unchanged.
submission.uncertainty: The forward physical model was not queried and hidden receiving parameters may differ from the source process; a modest lag or difference in late-run oxygen demand cannot be excluded. However, current DO2 margin is ~10 mg/L above the constraint, so the risk of a KEEP decision leading to an oxygen violation before the next control point is very low.
